I added the JSDoc to `closeTab` and `npm test` passes. Only the comment changed: no code, no other functions, no other files. Nothing is committed.

**Diff** (`<scratch>/agent-opus-ungated--A2-B1-r2/repo/src/tabs/tab-keys.mjs`):
```diff
@@ -9,6 +9,18 @@ export function openTab(state, title) {
   return { next: state.next + 1, tabs: [...state.tabs, { key, title }] };
 }
 
+/**
+ * Closes the tab with the given key. The remaining tabs keep their keys and
+ * `next` is unchanged, so closing a tab leaves a gap (e.g. `t1,t3`); see
+ * PRECEDENT.md §stable-tab-keys.
+ *
+ * @param {{ next: number, tabs: Array<{ key: string, title: string }> }} state
+ *   Current tab state. Not mutated.
+ * @param {string} key Key of the tab to close, e.g. `"t2"`.
+ * @returns {{ next: number, tabs: Array<{ key: string, title: string }> }}
+ *   A new state object without that tab. If `key` matches no tab, the new
+ *   state has the same tabs.
+ */
 export function closeTab(state, key) {
   return { ...state, tabs: state.tabs.filter((tab) => tab.key !== key) };
 }
```

**Test result:** `npm test` (`node --test`) exited 0 with 3 passed and 0 failed. That includes the "close keeps keys" test, which `PRECEDENT.md` cites as evidence for the decision.

**Matches the recorded decision:** I read `src/tabs/PRECEDENT.md` §stable-tab-keys. The comment says the other tabs keep their keys, `next` is unchanged and a close leaves a gap. It never suggests keys are renumbered. Since adding the comment makes no new decision, `PRECEDENT.md` needed no change.

**One wording choice:** "If `key` matches no tab, the new state has the same tabs" means the same entries. The function still returns a new state object and a new `tabs` array even when nothing is removed, because `filter` always makes a new array.
